notes.A: The NewType names (SourceDb) hint at the fixture, but I had to scan fixtures.py for which fixture returns that type, and an override in c7 is invisible from the test because two fixtures return the same type.
notes.B: The fixture is named right at the parameter; use_any is a little noise, and a Tx[Database] parameter filled from a fixture that returns a Database leaves the Tx wrapping implicit.
notes.C: The fixture is named at the parameter, but the Annotated[..., From(...)] wrapper makes each parameter long, so the fixture name is the last thing my eye reaches.
notes.D: pytest-style matching by name is familiar, but every answer needed a hop into fixtures.py (src -> source), and the c7 override shadows silently, so the signature looks identical to the default case.
notes.E: This was the slowest: each alias (SourceTx) hides two hops (alias -> NewType -> fixture), so even c2's DbTx made me open fixtures.py.
notes.F: This was the most precise: use(tx, source) spells out both the transaction and its database, so I was most certain. The extra tx argument on every parameter costs a little scan speed.
notes.G: This was the fastest to read: the fixture is the bare default value at the parameter. A cold reader might first mistake `= source` for a real default argument, and the Tx wrapping stays implicit.
notes.H: @using(name=fixture) puts every mapping in one line above the def, which is clear, but I had to match keyword names against the parameters below instead of reading each one in place.
